turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same n-i-p (regular) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".


The data files for this task are in your current working directory:
  - b3_pvk_stack_train.csv
  - b3_pvk_stack_pool.csv
Read them from disk. Give your answer as your final message — do not write it to a file.
turns.answer_text:
I've read both files. Let me analyze the training data patterns and match the pool candidates against the best-performing device recipes.

## Key patterns from the training data (top performers)

The highest-efficiency n-i-p MAPbI3 devices share: a TiO₂-c or SnO₂-based ETL (often with a fullerene/SnO₂ passivation interlayer for better band alignment and suppressed interface recombination), a doped Spiro-MeOTAD or PTAA hole-selective contact, and an Au/Ag back contact, typically with spin-coating-based absorber deposition:

- **20.85%**: FTO | TiO2-c | **SnO2-np** | Spiro-MeOTAD | Ag
- **19.35%**: FTO | TiO2-c | **PCBM-60** | PCDTBT1 | MoO3 | Au
- **18.9%**: FTO | TiO2-c | BaSnO3-np | **PTAA** | Au
- **18.19%**: ITO | **SnO2-np** | **PTAA** | Ag
- **17.9%**: ITO | **C60; Phlm | C60** | TaTm | F6-TCNNQ; TaTm | Au (Co-evaporation)
- **17.2%**: FTO | TiO2-c | **C60** | Spiro-MeOTAD | Ag
- **16.5%**: ITO | TiO2-c | **C60** | PTAA | Ag

Missing HTL/back contact, carbon-only contacts, DSSC-type electrolytes, and bare-metal substrates all score very low (<10%).

## Matching pool candidates to these recipes

- **c064** (FTO | TiO2-c | SnO2-np | Spiro-MeOTAD | Au): near-identical to the 20.85% champion stack (only Au vs Ag, spin vs spin>>dipp). SnO₂ overlayer passivates TiO₂/perovskite interface → excellent extraction, low recombination. Expect ~17–20%.
- **c005** (ITO | TiO2-c | PCBM-60 | PCDTBT8 | MoO3 | Au): near-exact match to the 19.35% device (PCDTBT8 vs PCDTBT1, same family). PCBM passivates TiO₂; MoO₃/Au gives clean hole contact. Expect ~17–19%.
- **c017** (ITO | C60; PhIm | C60 | TaTM | F6-TCNNQ; TaTm | Ag, Co-evaporation): essentially identical to the 17.9% co-evaporated device (Ag vs Au). Doped organic transport bilayers give superb selectivity. Expect ~17–18%.
- **c068** (ITO | SnO2-np | TiO2-np | PTAA | Au | MoO3): combines the SnO2-np/PTAA recipe (18.19%) with TiO₂-np and a MoO₃-capped contact (cf. 18.9% BaSnO3/PTAA/Au). Expect ~15–18%.
- **c073** (ITO-HMDS | TiO2-c | C60 | PTAA | Ag): direct match to the 16.5% device; C60 interlayer improves band alignment, PTAA is a top HTM. Expect ~15–17%.

Next-best (c080 ~ TiO2-c|C60/Spiro/Ag → 17.2% analog, c031, c043) are slightly less directly supported.

Final: c064, c005, c017, c068, c073
